cosmos500_0000.caption: A square color photograph taken from a direct top-down overhead angle looking straight down at a food factory packaging line, the full frame in sharp focus with deep depth of field so every mechanical joint and dumpling pleat reads clearly. Bright, diffuse industrial LED lighting floods downward from high ceiling fixtures, catching cool highlights along brushed stainless steel edges and casting small soft shadows directly beneath each object. The palette is clean and clinical: the matte white of the conveyor belt, the vivid molded blue of the plastic tray, the glossy black weave of carbon fiber, silvery steel, and the pale cream of flour-dusted dumplings. A stainless steel gantry frame spans the width of the line along the upper third of the image, its rectangular brushed-metal beams bolted at right angles, and from its center hangs a delta robot seen from above, three carbon-fiber parallel-link arms radiating outward in perfect symmetry at even one-hundred-twenty-degree spacing, each arm a straight paired-rod linkage with clean spherical joints, no twisted or crossed connections, all three converging on a small central circular hub. Beneath the hub a translucent silicone suction cup grips the domed top of a single dumpling, holding it suspended in mid-air a short distance above the belt, the cup visibly flexed against the dough, the lifted dumpling's pleats radiating naturally from its pinched crown with a light dusting of white flour still clinging to its ridges. The white conveyor belt runs horizontally across the middle of the frame carrying evenly spaced rows of uncooked dumplings, each one plump and crescent-shaped with hand-folded pleats and a fine powdery coating of flour that also sprinkles the belt surface in faint pale traces around them. At image-right sits a rectangular blue plastic tray in a three-by-four grid of twelve identical square compartments, each compartment cleanly countable, seven of them filled with neatly placed dumplings and five standing empty as smooth blue wells with slightly rounded corners. The suspended dumpling hangs on the direct path between its pickup point on the belt and one of the empty compartments, making the pick-and-place motion unmistakably in progress. The steel frame occludes a narrow strip of the belt at the top of the frame, the robot arms overlap the belt without touching it, and the tray sits fully visible with nothing crowding its edges. The style is crisp industrial documentary photography with high detail and true color, the mood precise, hygienic and quietly automated.

cosmos500_0001.caption: A square color photograph shows the interior of a mechanical assembly workshop, framed in a medium-wide shot at bench height from a slightly elevated three-quarter angle that looks obliquely along the axis of a horizontal steel shaft, with deep depth of field holding every component sharp from the gripper to the far ring. Cool white light from high-bay LED fixtures overhead falls from upper image-left, laying bright specular streaks along the machined steel, ringing a thin highlight along each rim, and casting the soft shadows of the arm and ring supports toward image-right across the benchtop. The palette is industrial: gunmetal gray on the robot arm, polished silver on the shaft, dark charcoal on the rings, worn olive-green paint on the steel workbench, and behind them a pale gray pegboard wall with black shelving uprights, a red tool cabinet, coiled yellow air hoses, and hanging wrench silhouettes slightly softened by distance. On image-left, an articulated robot arm with two jointed segments in matte scuffed paint, silver collars, and round rotary housings at its shoulder, elbow, and wrist is bolted with four silver hex bolts to a mounting plate on the workbench, a black cable clipped along its upper segment. The arm's three-jaw gripper holds the left end of the horizontal steel shaft, its knurled jaws visibly closed around the shaft's surface, the contact engaged and the shaft gripped level and motionless. From the gripper the shaft runs straight toward image-right, a ground cylinder as thick as a broom handle carrying a long reflected highlight, with a few loose hex nuts and a steel ruler resting on the near edge of the bench in the foreground beneath it. To the right of the gripper, two upright metal rings of identical diameter stand on separate support posts with triangular gussets, each post bolted to the bench and spaced a hand's width apart, each ring a flat charcoal annulus with a machined inner rim, their central holes sharing the shaft's axis. The shaft passes through both holes, and its right tip extends several inches beyond the farther ring, ending in a flat chamfered end face; clear gaps remain between the shaft and both inner rims, pale background showing through as an unbroken crescent at each ring, with no metal intersection anywhere. The front-to-back occlusion reads plainly: the gripper and shaft sit foremost, the shaft overlaps the rear inner edge of each hole while the front face of each ring frames it, and the nearer ring's post partially overlaps the farther one, all rendered in a crisp industrial documentary style with a methodical, precise, quietly mechanical mood.

cosmos500_0002.caption: A square color photograph shows a close-up, slightly elevated three-quarter view of an electronics workbench, the SCARA robot filling the central frame in crisp focus with a moderate depth of field that keeps the entire arm assembly sharp while the far edge of the bench softens gently. Bright, cool-white light from an LED task lamp at upper image-left rakes across the scene, throwing specular highlights along the anodized aluminum arm links and the gripper piston while casting soft shadows toward image-right across the matte gray ESD mat covering the tabletop. The palette pairs the matte black of the robot's pedestal and gripper jaws with the satin silver of its two arm links, the vivid solder-mask green of the circuit board, and small accents of gold, copper and white on the board's surface. In the background, the bench holds a compact soldering station with a coiled iron stand at image-left, a shallow parts tray of loose screws and standoffs near the rear edge, and a loose tangle of red and black test leads, while a pale birch plywood bench edge runs along the bottom of the frame. The SCARA robot rises from a cylindrical matte-black pedestal whose mounting flange is bolted to the tabletop with four silver hex-head bolts, one at each corner, and a short vertical shoulder column carries the first rotary joint. Extending horizontally from the shoulder, the first straight aluminum link reaches toward image-right, where a round elbow joint with a concentric pivot cap connects it to the second straight link, both links lying in a single level plane, rigid and unbent, meeting at a natural open angle of roughly one hundred twenty degrees with clean mechanical alignment at every pivot. At the wrist end of the second link, a compact pneumatic gripper hangs from a vertical Z-axis cylinder whose silver piston rod is extended partway down, its two black anodized jaws clamping the top edge of a single rectangular green circuit board patterned with fine copper traces, faint white silkscreen markings and a row of gold edge-connector fingers along its lower edge. The gripper is lowering the board into an open slot of a black backplane connector fixed to the tabletop directly below, the action caught mid-descent with the gold fingers already partway inside the slot's mouth while the upper half of the board remains above it, held level and vertical in the jaws. The second link partially occludes the shoulder joint behind it, the gripper body overlaps the board's top edge, and the board itself blocks the interior of the slot, giving clear, readable occlusion that separates each component in depth, and the picture carries the precise documentary clarity of technical product photography with the calm, methodical mood of automated assembly in progress.

cosmos500_0003.caption: A square color photograph presents a medium shot of a neighborhood bakery work counter, captured from a slightly elevated eye-level angle, with the white collaborative robot arm and the square cream cake in crisp focus at center frame while the back of the shop softens into a shallow blur. Warm daylight enters from a window at image-left, laying bright highlights along the brushed stainless steel countertop and across the arm's glossy white shell, while soft shadows stretch toward image-right beneath the cake board and the arm's mounting base. The palette ties ivory cream and clean white to the frosting and the robot housing, deep cocoa brown to the piped lettering, vivid red to the strawberries, and cool gray to the steel surfaces. The blurred background reads only as warm amber shelf light, the pale glow of a glass display case, and vague rounded loaves resting on wooden racks. The robot arm is fixed to the countertop at image-left on a circular bolted flange, its upper link rising to a single shoulder joint, a shorter forearm link descending from one elbow joint, and a compact wrist joint tilting the end effector so the gripped piping bag stands nearly vertical over the cake, three rotary joints in total with smooth cylindrical connections and no extra segments. The two-finger gripper cradles the bag's twisted white body, and the metal nozzle hovers a finger-width above the final letter, lifting away with a thin glossy tail of chocolate still connecting the tip to the finished stroke, the wrist angle matching the piping motion exactly. The square cream cake sits slightly image-right of center on a white board, its smooth ivory buttercream carrying the words "Happy 80th, Grandma Lin" piped in two neat lines of dark chocolate across the top surface, every stroke of even thickness with clean rounded ends and accurate spelling. Beside the cake at image-right sit a clear glass bowl of glossy red strawberries with fresh green hulls and a spatula lying flat, its stainless blade faintly smeared with cream and its light wooden handle angled toward the foreground corner. The arm leans over the cake without occluding the lettering, the bowl and spatula rest clear of the cake's edge, and the counter's reflective sheen softly mirrors the white links above it. The style is clean documentary realism with a warm, careful, celebratory mood.

cosmos500_0004.caption: A square color photograph of the interior of a small foundry, framed at eye level in a medium-wide shot with the articulated robot arm centered, the sand mold below it and the far wall visible behind, rendered in sharp focus from foreground floor to back wall with a deep depth of field. Overhead tungsten work lamps hang from a dark steel truss ceiling and cast a hard warm light downward, while the pour itself throws an intense orange-white glow that rims the crucible's lip, catches the machined edges of the arm's joints and lays long soft shadows of the pedestal and mold across the floor away from the light. The palette is dominated by charcoal gray cinder block, the pale gray of raw concrete, the dull industrial yellow of the robot arm's housing and the blazing white-orange of the molten aluminum against the dark brown-black of the sand molds. Along the rear wall, empty molds are arranged in a row on the floor and on a low steel rack, their open rectangular cavities showing fresh dark sand, their wooden flasks stacked beside scattered hand tools and a coiled cable on the oil-stained concrete. The articulated robot arm is bolted to a square concrete pedestal at image-left with four heavy anchor bolts visible at its base, its yellow-enameled segments rising through two angled joints to a wrist positioned directly above the crucible, the wrist joint rotated so the end effector hangs over the vessel's top. The arm's clamp grips a welded steel cradle that cradles the thick-walled ceramic crucible, its gray-white refractory surface heat-stained and cracked at the rim, and the cradle holds the crucible tilted partway with its mouth angled down toward the sand mold below at image-right. A continuous stream of molten aluminum falls from the crucible's lip in a bright unbroken ribbon, glowing white at the pour point and shading to orange as it descends into the mold's pouring basin, where the liquid pools and spatters small glowing droplets against the dark sand. The crucible's body occludes part of the wall behind it, the arm's forearm crosses in front of the row of empty molds, and the basin's rim sits close beneath the falling stream with a hand's width of clearance, establishing the depth order of arm over cradle over mold. The photograph carries the clean documentary style of industrial editorial photography, and the scene's mood is one of controlled heat and mechanical precision frozen at the height of the pour.

cosmos500_0005.caption: A square color photograph presents a medium close-up of a surgical robot arm at work in an operating room, shot from a slightly elevated three-quarter angle at roughly table height, with crisp focus on the needle and incision and a softly blurred background. Brilliant cool-white light pours down from a large circular surgical lamp overhead, throwing bright specular highlights along the arm's metal joints and the needle's polished curve while soft shadows pool beneath the arm's housing and along the folded edges of the drapes. The palette is dominated by sterile whites and cool grays on the robot, deep teal green on the surgical drapes, pale silvery steel on the instruments, and a narrow band of warm pinkish skin exposed at the center of the field. The background dissolves into soft shapes of mint-green wall panels, the glowing rim of the overhead light array, the faint outlines of monitor screens and an anesthesia cart, and the blurred teal shoulder of a gowned figure standing at the far side of the table. In the right half of the frame the robot arm rises from a heavy rectangular white base bolted to a pedestal at image-right, its segmented links articulated in a smooth upward arc, each joint ringed with brushed-metal collars and small status lights glowing green. The arm terminates in a compact wrist mechanism whose needle driver, a pair of slim steel forceps with fine serrated jaws, is gripping a curved suture needle at its midpoint, the silvery crescent angled downward with its sharp tip pointing toward the incision and a length of dark blue monofilament thread trailing from its swaged end in a gentle curve. The needle driver hovers above a draped incision at center-left: the patient is covered in layered teal surgical drapes whose rectangular fenestration exposes a small oval of skin bearing a neat three-centimeter incision line, two fine interrupted sutures already placed and knotted beside the entry point where the needle is descending. The robot arm's wrist is rotated slightly so the needle's curve aligns with the incision's edge, and the taut thread between the needle and the last placed stitch shows the suturing actively in progress, the metal of the driver gleaming against the matte fabric of the drape. The base of the robot sits lower and farther back than the operative field, so the arm reaches over the draped body without touching it, and the needle, driver, and incision all remain fully visible and unobstructed. The image carries the clean, high-clarity look of clinical documentary photography, with a calm, precise, quietly intense mood of concentrated technological care.

cosmos500_0006.caption: A square color photograph shows a bicycle frame welding workshop in a medium shot at standing eye level, the robot arm and the titanium frame filling the center of the composition with the workshop interior receding behind them in crisp focus. The dominant light is the welding arc itself, a blue-white point of intense brilliance at the bottom-bracket joint that throws cool highlights across the titanium tubing, the steel jig and the robot arm's painted housings, casts hard consistent shadows away from the contact point across the concrete floor, and leaves the far corners of the shop in dim amber gloom from two overhead sodium lamps. The palette is built from the gunmetal grey of machinery, the pale matte silver of titanium, the safety yellow of the robot arm, and the hot oranges and electric blues radiating from the arc and the falling sparks. Behind the work cell, a perforated steel pegboard holds rows of hand tools, a metal shelving unit stacked with tubing and wire spools stands against a cinderblock wall, and a dark green welding curtain hangs from a ceiling rail, while the foreground shows grey concrete scored with expansion joints and painted with a ring of yellow-and-black hazard chevrons marking the robot's working envelope. Bolted to a heavy square steel base plate anchored to the floor at image-left with four thick hex-head anchor bolts, a safety-yellow articulated robot arm rises and reaches diagonally across the scene, its three jointed segments linked by dark rotary housings, a black corrugated cable conduit running along its spine to the welding torch gripped in its wrist. At image-right, the titanium bicycle frame sits clamped in a black anodised aluminium jig, its brushed grey top tube, down tube and seat tube converging on the cylindrical bottom-bracket shell, the completed half of the circumferential weld showing a neat rippled bead edged with faint heat tint in bands of straw and blue. The arm is actively welding, its copper-tipped torch nozzle pressed in direct contact with the bottom-bracket joint, the arc flashing in a concentrated blue-white bloom around a small molten pool glowing orange at the seam, the fresh bead visibly extended partway around the shell. A fan of sparks falls from the point of contact, frozen mid-descent as bright orange streaks and discrete glowing particles, the longest trails reaching the concrete where a few fresh sparks scatter and bounce, while a thin wisp of pale smoke rises past the seat tube. The robot's forearm and torch occlude the near edge of the down tube while the jig stands slightly behind the arm's base, and every highlight and shadow in the scene agrees with the arc's position, giving the image the sharp, high-contrast precision of industrial documentary photography with a moody, concentrated atmosphere.

cosmos500_0007.caption: A square color photograph shows a medium close-up of a laboratory bench at a slightly elevated three-quarter camera angle, with moderate depth of field keeping the robotic arm, pipette, and vial in crisp focus while the rear of the bench falls softly out of focus, and the front edge of the benchtop runs along the bottom of the frame. Cool white light from an overhead LED panel toward image-left strikes the scene, catching bright highlights along brushed aluminum edges and the glass rim of the vial, casting short soft shadows to image-right across the benchtop, while a weaker fill from image-right keeps the shaded faces of the joints readable. The palette is clinical and cool: silvery metal and matte black on the arm, a black epoxy resin tabletop with a faint speckled texture, the clear colorless glass of the vial, and a pale blue liquid visible inside it, with soft gray and white blurs behind. The background resolves only into vague shapes of shelving, stacked glassware, and a pale wall, rendered as gentle washes of cool light without sharp detail. Bolted to the tabletop at image-left, the robotic arm rises from a circular steel mounting flange secured by four visible hex bolts, its first segment a matte black vertical column housing a rotary base joint, leading into a brushed aluminum upper arm with a cylindrical shoulder actuator whose circular joint cover shows a concentric seam, then an elbow hinge with a visible silver pivot pin and a black cable loom clipped along the underside of each segment, and finally a compact wrist of two stacked servo housings, each joint's rotation axis set perpendicular to its neighbor so the whole chain reads as mechanically plausible. The wrist's two-finger parallel gripper, its small jaws faced with dark rubber pads, clamps the barrel of a clear disposable pipette marked with fine graduation lines, holding it upright as the arm is lowering it toward a small open glass vial standing on the bench to image-right of the base, the pipette's tapered translucent tip centered exactly above the vial's circular mouth with a single bead of pale blue liquid suspended at the orifice. The vial's removed black screw cap rests flat on the benchtop beside it, the vial partially occludes the arm's lower column, and the wrist and gripper overlap the soft background, while the arm stands roughly twice the vial's height and the gap between tip and rim reads as only a few centimeters on a shared vertical line. In the immediate foreground the benchtop sits empty, its matte surface catching a faint reflected sheen of the overhead light. The overall style is precise documentary realism with a clean, quiet, methodical mood.

cosmos500_0008.caption: A square color photograph shows a fixed-base articulated palletizing robot actively lowering a corrugated cardboard box toward a wooden pallet in a warehouse corner, framed from a slightly elevated three-quarter viewpoint at about chest height with the robot base, the full articulated arm, the descending box and the entire stacked pallet held in sharp focus under a deep depth of field. Cool white light from overhead LED high-bay fixtures falls from above and slightly image-left, tracing bright highlights along the robot's painted steel arm, the metal gripper plate and the taped seams of the cardboard boxes, while soft shadows pool toward image-right across the concrete floor and beneath the pallet's lower boards. The palette is industrial and muted: safety-orange robot steel, kraft-brown corrugated cardboard with dark tan packing-tape strips, pale unfinished pine pallet wood, and smooth grey concrete on both floor and walls. The setting is the junction of two grey concrete block walls meeting at a vertical corner directly behind the pallet, their mortar lines and faint dust streaks visible, with floor expansion joints and a yellow painted safety square marking the robot cell and dark steel racking holding shrink-wrapped goods standing further back. On image-left the robot's heavy cast pedestal sits bolted flat to the concrete with four visible anchor bolts, its rotary column rising into a shoulder joint tilted slightly forward, an upper arm angling down, an elbow bent at a natural working angle, and a wrist pitching downward, with a black cable conduit clipped along the arm's spine so the whole linkage reaches over the pallet without strain. At the wrist a flat rectangular vacuum gripper plate carrying a row of round rubber suction cups presses flush against the top face of the new corrugated box, the cups seated with full contact, and the box hangs suspended mid-descent a few centimeters above the left slot of the forming third layer, its taped top seam and bottom edges parallel to the boxes beneath it and visibly closing the gap. On the wooden pallet at image-right, six kraft-brown cardboard boxes sit fully supported in two aligned layers of three: the lower layer runs lengthwise along the pallet with side edges flush against one another, and the upper layer lies perpendicular to the lower so the staggered, alternating bond is clearly readable, every box resting squarely on the layer below with no gaps and the whole stack aligned with the pallet's deck boards and stringers. The descending box matches the orientation of the first layer and aims into the empty left position above the second layer, its projected footprint aligned with the stack's outer edges, while the robot base occupies the image-left foreground, the pallet anchors image-right, and the arm spans between them, partially overlapping the corner wall behind. The plain boxes carry no lettering, and the picture reads as crisp documentary industrial realism with clean, squared geometry and a precise, orderly, mechanical mood.

cosmos500_0009.caption: A square color photograph captures a collaborative robotic arm glazing pottery in a workshop, framed in a medium close-up at table height with a shallow depth of field that keeps the arm, gripper, bowl, and glaze surface tack-sharp while the background softens into muted shapes. Warm natural light enters from a window at image-left, casting soft highlights along the arm's matte off-white shell and the liquid glaze, with gentle shadows falling toward image-right across the bench. The palette centers on warm honey-brown wood, the cool off-white and light gray of the cobot, the pale terra-cotta pink of the unglazed clay, and the dense creamy white of the glaze. Behind the bench, blurred shelving holds out-of-focus rows of clay pots in soft tan and gray tones beside the vague glow of a window, suggesting a working studio without sharp detail. In the foreground, a heavy wooden workbench fills the lower half of the frame, its planks showing grain, faint clay dust, and scuffed patina. Bolted to the bench top near image-left is the cobot's circular metal base, its jointed arm rising and arching toward image-right in a smooth curve of rounded white segments with dark seams at each joint. At the wrist, a three-finger gripper of brushed steel and dark rubber-tipped digits clasps the unglazed bowl by its foot ring, the three curved fingers spaced evenly around the ring and making clean contact with the dry clay surface, each fingertip resting against it without intersecting the ceramic. The bowl hangs mouth-down beneath the gripper, its unglazed body showing the fine matte texture of bisque-fired clay in pale pinkish tan, and its rim is submerged partway into a wide container of thick white glaze sitting on the bench below. The glaze's surface is broken by the dipping, with slow ripples spreading outward from the rim and a raised wet meniscus where liquid meets clay, while heavy drips of white glaze fall from the bowl's rim edge, one drop mid-air beneath the lip and another stretching into a thread back to the bath. The arm, bowl, and container align in a clear vertical path with no overlap between gripper and glaze surface, the bowl held level and fully visible. The style is clean documentary product photography with realistic textures and naturalistic color, and the mood is calm, precise, and industrious, the quiet meeting of handcraft and automation frozen at the exact moment of the dip.

cosmos500_0010.caption: A square color photograph captures the interior of a furniture workshop, framed at eye level in a medium shot with deep focus that holds both the machinery and the surrounding room sharp. Warm overhead pendant lamps hang from a high, exposed-beam ceiling, casting amber light downward and drawing bright highlights along the robot arm's housings, while softer daylight enters through tall windows on image-left, laying pale diagonal bands across the concrete floor and throwing soft shadows of the arm and workbench toward image-right. The palette mixes the cool grey of poured concrete and charcoal machinery with the warm honey tones of sawn lumber, tan sawdust, and the amber glow of the lamps. The background shows cluttered workshop shelving stacked with timber planks, clamps, and toolboxes against a brick wall, with a bandsaw and a dust-collection hose coiled at image-right, all rendered with crisp textural detail. At image-left foreground, an articulated robot arm with four visible jointed segments is bolted to a heavy cylindrical steel pedestal anchored to the floor with four dark hex bolts, its base plate slightly scuffed and dust-filmed. The arm's segments are painted matte charcoal grey with a single safety-yellow wrist band, each elbow joint caught mid-flex as the arm reaches inward across the frame. Its end effector carries a circular orbital sanding pad that presses firmly against the curved wooden chair back, the pad's face flattened against the wood in active sanding contact, a faint halo of fresh dust rising off the abrasion point. The chair back, clamped upright on a heavy oak workbench by two steel bar clamps with black rubber pads, curves in a smooth bow of pale maple with visible grain lines, its surface showing a contrast between darker unsanded arcs and a lighter freshly sanded band directly beneath the pad. Fine sawdust collects beneath the chair in a soft tan ridge along the benchtop, dusting the clamp feet and drifting over the workbench edge onto the concrete below. The robot arm overlaps the workbench in depth, its wrist closest to the chair, while the chair back sits centered slightly image-right, facing the arm at an angle that shows both its curve and the active contact point. The overall mood is industrious and precise, the photograph rendered in a realistic, documentary style with clean mechanical surfaces, warm wood textures, and the suspended quality of work in progress.

cosmos500_0011.caption: A square color photograph frames a medium close-up of a greenhouse propagation bench from a slightly elevated three-quarter angle, with deep depth of field keeping the robot arm, seedling, terracotta pot and seedling tray uniformly sharp from foreground to midground. Soft diffused daylight enters through the translucent polycarbonate roof and the image-left wall, casting a neutral white illumination that puts gentle highlights on the arm's anodized aluminum segments and the pot's flared rim while dropping soft shadows toward image-right across the bench slats. The palette pairs the warm orange of the terracotta pot with the dark chocolate brown of the moist potting soil, the vivid green of the tomato seedling's leaves, the silvery gray and white of the robot arm, and the matte gray of the plastic tray. Behind the bench, greenhouse rows recede in detail: parallel aluminum benches carrying trays of young plants, black irrigation lines on overhead rails, and a ribbed polycarbonate ceiling held by white-painted steel trusses, while the foreground bench surface is galvanized steel slatting scattered with crumbs of soil and fine water droplets. The collaborative robot arm is bolted to the bench edge at image-left on a square steel mounting plate with four visible hex bolts, its articulated white-and-gray segments bending down over the bench with a black cable clipped along its spine and its wrist angled vertically above the pot. The arm is actively lowering the seedling: its two-fingered soft gripper, fitted with cream silicone pads, holds the seedling's cylindrical brown root plug by its sides, the pads making gentle contact with the plug only, leaving the slender green stem rising uncompressed and unbent between the fingertips while the paired rounded cotyledons and small serrated true leaves remain upright and alert. The plug hangs partway through its descent, its flat bottom hovering a few centimeters above a pre-dibbled cylindrical soil hole in the terracotta pot at center-right, the plug's vertical axis centered exactly over the hole's dark opening so the alignment reads plainly, with a few loose crumbs of soil resting on the rim. Beside the pot on image-right sits the gray plastic seedling tray, its four-by-six grid of square cells holding several similar tomato seedlings in brown plugs alongside a few emptied cells, the tray overlapping slightly behind the pot while the arm enters from image-left with the gripper and plug suspended above the pot without touching its rim. The mood is calm, precise and industrious, rendered in a clean documentary style that emphasizes the delicacy of automated horticulture.

cosmos500_0012.caption: A square color photograph of an automotive assembly shop interior, captured at eye level in a medium shot with crisp focus across the robot arm and windshield and mild softness toward the far end of the production hall. Overhead rows of high-bay LED fixtures cast cool white light downward, catching bright highlights along the robot's painted steel joints and the curved glass surface, while soft shadows pool beneath the pedestal base and under the windshield's lower edge. The palette is dominated by the safety-orange enamel of the robot arm, the glossy black of the fresh sealant bead, the pale smoke-grey tint of the windshield glass, and the concrete grey of the factory floor marked with yellow lane lines. In the background, the assembly shop stretches into gentle blur: grey steel columns, hanging cable reels, conveyor sections, and the faint shapes of vehicle bodies on the line, all rendered as soft industrial forms without fine detail. In the foreground at image-right, a six-axis robot arm is bolted to a heavy grey steel floor pedestal anchored with visible hex bolts, its articulated segments of orange and gunmetal extending upward and across the frame, each rotary joint and wrist axis clearly defined, with bundled black and blue pneumatic hoses running along its upper arm. The arm's wrist terminates in a dispensing gun with a metal nozzle and black cartridge body, and the gun is extruding a continuous bead of black sealant, the nozzle pressed against the glass edge with a fresh glossy ribbon emerging from the tip and joining the unbroken bead already laid down. The bead traces the perimeter of an upright windshield held vertically in a grey metal fixture at image-left, the thick dark line running cleanly along the lower edge and turning up the side pillar, ending exactly at the nozzle's current contact point roughly two-thirds up the image-right edge, while the remaining upper arc of glass still shows bare clear surface awaiting the bead. The windshield's laminated glass catches a soft vertical reflection of the ceiling lights, and a faint dotted frit band borders its inner edge beneath the sealant path. The robot's elbow bends partway through its programmed arc, joints angled in active motion along the windshield's contour. The style is clean industrial documentary photography with high detail and even exposure, and the mood is precise, automated, and quietly methodical.

cosmos500_0013.caption: A square color photograph of a recycling sorting plant interior, captured at eye level in a medium-wide shot with deep depth of field that keeps the machinery, conveyor and bin all in sharp focus. Overhead industrial LED high-bay fixtures cast cool white light down across the scene, catching bright specular highlights along the brushed aluminum joints of the robot arm and the silver rims of the cans, while soft shadows pool beneath the conveyor frame and under the steel base on the gray epoxy concrete floor. The dominant palette mixes the matte safety yellow of the articulated robot arm with the dull galvanized gray of the conveyor, the translucent blue-green tint of the plastic bottle, the silver of the aluminum cans and the green-painted steel of the sorting bin. In the background, corrugated metal wall panels, hanging cable trays, stacked plastic crates and a second conveyor line recede toward a roll-up loading door, all rendered in muted grays and industrial greens. Image-center, a six-axis articulated robot arm with visible rotary joints, black cabling run along its segments and a wrist-mounted vacuum gripper is bolted through four heavy hex anchor bolts to a rectangular steel base plate beside the conveyor, its yellow paint chipped slightly at the edges to reveal darker primer. The arm is actively lifting a flattened clear plastic bottle, the ribbed PET container creased and collapsed, held by a round black rubber suction cup sealed against its side, suspended several inches above the moving belt mid-path on its arc toward the bin, with a faint streak of motion in its crinkled transparent surface. The black rubber belt of the conveyor runs from image-left toward image-center, crowded with crumpled and dented aluminum cans in silver, red and faded blue, some still showing fragments of printed branding, scattered across the ribbed belt between stainless steel side rails. Image-right, the robot's gripper hangs above the open rim of a waist-high green steel sorting bin with a welded white stencil label plate riveted to its front panel reading "PET" in bold black capital letters, the bottle angled directly over its mouth so the transfer reads as underway. The steel base sits between the conveyor frame and the bin, the arm bridging the gap so the gripper clears the belt's edge by a hand's width, the cans below left untouched and spatially separated from the lifted bottle. The visual style is clean industrial documentary photography with crisp mechanical detail, cool color temperature and a mood of automated, methodical efficiency.

cosmos500_0014.caption: A square color photograph of a low wheeled mobile robot transporting a lidded plastic tote along a concrete warehouse aisle, framed in a slightly elevated three-quarter view from chest height with a deep depth of field that keeps the robot, the floor beneath it and the flanking storage racks in sharp focus. Cool white light from a row of high-bay LED fixtures overhead falls straight down the aisle, catching bright highlights on the tote's lid and along the edges of the brushed metal chassis while laying soft shadows directly under the robot's body and at the foot of every rack post, with faint reflections sheening on the sealed concrete. The palette is industrial and muted: pale gray concrete scored with darker saw-cut lines, silver-gray galvanized rack uprights with orange horizontal beams, a slate-blue tote with a light gray lid, a charcoal chassis, matte black rubber tires and vivid yellow steel guards. Behind the robot the aisle recedes between tall storage racks on image-left and image-right, their beams loaded with cardboard cartons, plastic bins and shrink-wrapped pallets, the uprights and boxes diminishing toward a bright loading area at the far end. The robot is a rectangular metal chassis with rounded corners riding low on exposed rubber drive wheels, each tire's tread pressing visibly flat against the concrete with natural weight, its side panels seamed and fastened with hex bolts, a narrow status light strip glowing green, and a dark rubber bumper strip running the full width of its front edge. The lidded plastic tote rests inside a recessed cargo platform set into the top of the chassis, its ribbed walls rising from a base boxed in by low metal retaining stops at all four corners, the load reading as firmly supported with no floating components while the lid's rim and recessed handholds catch the overhead light. A compact lidar sensor sits on a short black bracket mounted at the front of the platform ahead of the tote, its domed housing raised just clear of the lid line so the scanning area around it stays completely unobstructed by cargo. Travelling diagonally toward the image-right foreground, the robot's front wheels sit partway across a shallow floor joint, a dark narrow groove between slabs, while its rear wheels remain on the near section, the axles straight and undistorted, the chassis level, and clear visible clearance between its side panels and the yellow protective guards bolted around the nearest rack posts on both sides of the aisle. The overall impression is of a credible working warehouse operation: mechanically coherent structure, honest tire contact with the floor, clear load support relationships and crisp functional detail under calm, even lighting.

cosmos500_0015.caption: A square color photograph shows a stair-climbing delivery robot actively ascending an outdoor concrete stairway, framed full-body in a three-quarter side view from camera height level with the chassis, with the robot centered and several worn steps visible above and below for spatial context. Deep focus keeps the track contacts, chassis, linkage, and cargo box sharp, while late-afternoon sunlight enters from upper image-left as warm, moderately hard light, catching aluminum pivot pins, the cargo box rim, and the edges of rubber tread lugs, and throwing crisp shadows toward lower image-right across the concrete risers. The palette is dominated by mineral gray concrete with beige aggregate and darker moisture stains, charcoal-black track rubber, a matte light-gray cargo box with a slightly darker lid, safety-yellow chassis panels, blue anodized leveling arms, a black steel railing at image-right, and muted red brick and green foliage at the upper landing. The stairway rises from lower image-right foreground to upper image-left background, its steps showing square nosings, hairline cracks, embedded anti-slip strips, expansion joints, and fine grit along the edges; a brick wall closes image-left, the railing runs parallel to the slope at image-right without crossing the robot, and the top landing opens to sky and leaves. The robot is mid-climb, not parked: a front triangular track module and a rear triangular track module are pressed against adjacent step edges, their rubber treads visibly compressed over the nosings with small dust at the contact patches, the lower module carrying load on the lower edge while the upper module bites the next edge, so the chassis tilts parallel to the stair slope at about thirty-two degrees. The top cargo box stays level through a leveling linkage: two blue arms and a short silver actuator connect box to chassis with one pivot extended and one pivot partway turned, holding the box top parallel to the landing while its underside remains supported by a clear load path into the tilted frame rather than hovering. The near modules occlude small portions of the risers they touch, the box overlaps the upper chassis without hiding the linkage, and clear air gaps remain between tread blocks, brackets, step nosings, and panel seams, with every contact bearing weight naturally. The style is realistic documentary product photography with exact engineering detail, clean geometry, plausible gravity, and a quiet mood of efficient motion upward.

cosmos500_0016.caption: A square color photograph shows an autonomous floor-scrubbing robot working along the central aisle between rows of seats in an airport terminal, captured at a low three-quarter angle from behind the machine with the whole robot, its wet trail, and the floor ahead in sharp focus. Bright even illumination comes from long rectangular ceiling light panels running the length of the concourse, their cool white glow reflecting off the polished floor, while soft shadows gather beneath the seat rows on image-left and image-right. The palette is dominated by the terminal's light gray stone flooring, the white housing of the robot, the dark charcoal seat cushions with silver steel frames, and the saturated yellow of a warning sign standing on the floor ahead. The terminal recedes into a background of repeating seat banks, each row of three contoured seats linked by shared armrests, distant glass curtain walls admitting pale daylight, and a high white ceiling carrying rows of the lit rectangular panels. The robot is a white square housing with gently rounded corners and a smooth matte finish, its top panel carrying a round black lidar turret at the center and a glowing blue light strip running along the front edge, the strip lit in a steady cyan-blue. Beneath the housing's leading edge, a dark disc brush is visibly engaged with the floor, its gray bristles splayed flat against the stone in active scrubbing contact, ringed by a thin halo of white cleaning foam at the brush rim. Behind the robot, its rear rubber squeegee presses the floor and leaves a wet reflective strip trailing down the aisle, the damp surface mirror-glossy and carrying elongated inverted reflections of the same rectangular ceiling panels, their spacing and alignment matching the lights overhead. A clear wet-dry boundary crosses the aisle at a shallow diagonal, dry matte gray floor ahead of the robot giving way to the darker saturated sheen of the freshly scrubbed strip behind it, the transition line sharp and unbroken. A folding yellow plastic A-frame sign stands on the dry floor ahead of the robot, printed in bold black capitals reading "CAUTION WET FLOOR" facing the camera. The machine sits centered in the aisle with seat rows flanking it in converging perspective, its wet trail narrowing toward the bottom of the frame. The style is crisp documentary realism with commercial-brochure clarity, the mood quiet, orderly and faintly futuristic.

cosmos500_0017.caption: A square color photograph of a wheeled mowing robot cutting grass beside a garden fence, shot at a low three-quarter angle near ground level with sharp focus carried from the turf under its wheels back to the fence pickets. Warm late-afternoon sunlight enters from image-left, moderately hard, laying a bright elongated highlight along the robot's glossy domed shell while its soft shadow and the long shadows of the fence rails stretch toward image-right across the lawn. The palette is dominated by the saturated greens of the grass, set against the clean white and light gray of the machine, the honey-brown weathered wood of the fence, and the dark charcoal of the tires. The background holds the garden fence running diagonally from the image-left edge toward image-right, its vertical wooden pickets warm brown with visible grain and pale knots, two horizontal rails, and a narrow bed of dark mulch with low leafy shrubs at its base; the foreground is a close lawn divided between a neat, freshly cut strip trailing behind the robot and taller, uncut blades lying ahead of it. The robot is a compact machine with a rounded housing of glossy white plastic, a light-gray rubber bumper skirt ringing its base, a dark sensor window on its front curve, a recessed carrying handle on top, and a small amber status light glowing beside it, and printed on the side panel facing the camera are the crisp black Chinese characters "作业中" in a clean sans-serif typeface, fully legible against the white shell. The machine is actively cutting: a fine spray of green clippings is flung from beneath its rear deck, blades at its front edge bend toward the housing, and the trimmed band behind it is visibly shorter and paler than the grass ahead. Its two visible wheels are rugged dark-gray rubber with deep chevron treads, both firmly grounded and pressed into the turf, flattening the grass beneath their contact patches, with faint soil stains on the sidewalls and small dark shadows pooling where the rubber meets the ground. The robot sits right of center, angled slightly toward image-left and tracking parallel to the fence line a hand's width from the mulch bed, its rounded body fully within the frame and unoccluded. The overall style is clean, realistic product photography, and the picture carries a calm, industrious mood of quiet automated work in a sunny garden.

cosmos500_0018.caption: A square color photograph shows a compact tracked inspection robot advancing through a drained brick sewer, framed in a medium shot from a low three-quarter front angle at track height, with sharp focus on the robot and its immediate surroundings while the tunnel recedes naturally into darkness behind it. Cool white light from a small LED ring around the robot's raised camera mixes with a soft source ahead of the frame, catching highlights along the damp brickwork and the machine's metal edges while soft shadows fall behind the chassis and beneath the tracks opposite the light. The palette runs from the warm red-brown of aged brick and the dark grey-brown of wet silt to the gunmetal grey of the robot's sealed body and the matte black of its rubber tracks. The cylindrical tunnel is built of weathered red brick with dark recessed mortar lines, patches of water staining and a faint damp sheen along its curved walls, the floor covered in a thin even layer of silt with only a narrow moist channel along the center invert before the passage dissolves into deep shadow. Positioned slightly image-left of center, the robot has a compact sealed metal body of brushed gunmetal panels with visible seam lines, flush screws and a rubber gasket around its midsection, mounted between two rubber tracks whose individual links are evenly shaped and correctly proportioned, every tread block in full contact with the ground. At the front of the chassis a short black mast raises a small camera above the body, its glass lens aimed down the tunnel with a status LED glowing beside it. The robot is actively advancing, its tracks pressing into the thin silt and squeezing shallow ridges of displaced sediment along their outer edges, while behind it a pair of continuous tread marks runs in straight parallel lines back toward the tunnel's dark mouth, recording the distance already travelled. To image-right of the robot a single fallen brick rests on the silt beside it, clearly outside the machine's path, separated from the nearest track by a strip of undisturbed sediment so the brick and the robot never overlap. The composition keeps the robot, its tread trail and the fallen brick fully visible and uncropped beneath the symmetrically curving walls, rendered in a photorealistic style with accurate mechanical proportions, readable chassis structure, realistic track contact and undistorted track links, carrying a quiet, methodical mood of solitary underground inspection.

cosmos500_0019.caption: A square color photograph of a compact hotel delivery robot mid-dock at a wall charger recessed into a charging niche along an upscale hotel corridor, framed in a medium shot from a slightly low camera height at the robot's own level, with the robot and niche in crisp focus and the corridor behind rendered in a mild depth-of-field softness. Warm recessed ceiling downlights cast pools of soft amber light along the corridor, while a cool white LED strip hidden in the niche's upper lip washes down over the charger, catching a bright highlight on the robot's glossy shell and throwing a short soft shadow behind it onto the niche's rear wall. The palette runs warm and neutral: champagne-beige wall panels, a charcoal-grey robot body, brushed stainless-steel charger hardware, and a carpeted corridor floor in muted taupe with a faint geometric pattern, punctuated by the saturated yellow of painted floor marks and the green glow of a status light. The corridor recedes toward image-left, its soft-focus depth showing only blurred door shapes, warm sconce glows and a distant corridor bend, while the charging niche sits at image-right, a clean rectangular recess lined in dark wood-effect laminate with the wall charger mounted flat against its back panel. The robot, roughly knee-height, is a rounded rectangular unit with a curved white front face, a dark tinted lid compartment on top, a narrow black sensor band across its upper edge, and two small drive wheels visible at its base; its body is angled square to the wall, actively docking, its rear charging electrodes pressed flush against the charger's two spring-loaded metal contact plates with the contact made and a ring of green LED light lit around the charger interface confirming the connection. No cable is in sight anywhere in the scene: the charger is a clean flush plate with no cord, tether or plug, and the floor around the niche is bare of wiring. The robot's wheels sit fully within a painted yellow rectangular floor mark on the niche's hard vinyl flooring, the parallel yellow guide lines and corner ticks framing both wheels evenly with even clearance on every side, the robot's stance settled and aligned. Above the niche, a small brushed-metal plaque carries the lettering "CHARGING" in dark capitals, and a tiny green indicator dot glows on the charger plate beside the electrode contact. The robot's pale front face is turned slightly toward the viewer, occluding nothing of the contact point, which remains fully visible between its rear housing and the wall plate. The visual style is clean commercial interior photography with accurate reflections, crisp edges on the niche and robot, and a calm, orderly mood of quiet automated routine in an empty corridor.

cosmos500_0020.caption: A square color photograph of a tracked-chassis mobile robot stopped mid-aisle in a commercial strawberry greenhouse, framed at chest height in a medium shot from a slight three-quarter angle showing the chassis flank and front corner, deep focus keeping racks, robot and gripper sharp across the frame. Cool diffuse daylight filters through the translucent ridge roof and pale steel trusses overhead, faint condensation beading on the inner glazing, the even illumination wrapping the foliage while bright highlights skim the robot's brushed aluminum arm and thin soft shadows lie beneath its chassis on the gray concrete walkway; the palette runs from deep leafy green and matte charcoal gray through silver metal to the saturated red of ripe fruit. Elevated strawberry racks line both image-left and image-right of the aisle in long parallel runs, white PVC gutters on galvanized frames carrying dense plants with serrated trifoliate leaves, small white five-petaled blossoms and clusters of glossy red berries dangling over the gutter edges toward the walkway, black irrigation tubing clipped along each gutter lip, the rows receding toward a distant end wall with a closed louvered vent fan. The robot sits between the racks as a low rectangular chassis riding on two continuous rubber tracks with deep chevron treads and visible drive sprockets, a brushed steel top plate, a small amber status lamp glowing at its front corner and a compact sensor pod above the nose. Behind the arm, a rear-mounted collection crate of translucent white plastic sits on the cargo deck, its lattice sides revealing a half full load of roughly two dozen harvested red strawberries heaped loosely with their green caps facing up and a light natural bloom on their surfaces. The arm-to-chassis joint is shown plainly and left fully unobstructed: a large circular rotary base bolted to the top plate with a ring of hex-head flange bolts, bundled black cables looping from the base into the first link. From this base the six-axis arm extends diagonally upward toward image-left, six articulated joints visible along its silver links, each marked by a darker rotating collar and clipped black cable looms, the arm caught mid-extension with the elbow raised and the wrist rolled partway toward the target berry. At the wrist, a soft three-fingered gripper of pale silicone is cradling one plump red strawberry, the padded fingers making gentle, even contact with the berry's seeded crimson surface without dimpling it, the green calyx flat and the stem straight and undistorted, the berry hanging just clear of the gutter as the pick proceeds, a small depth camera mounted beside the gripper. The picture reads as crisp documentary industrial photography, its mood methodical, clean and quietly industrious.

cosmos500_0021.caption: A square color photograph shows a wheeled sand-cleaning robot advancing along the wet tideline of a sandy beach, framed in a side three-quarter view from a low camera height near sand level, the entire machine in sharp focus and the shoreline behind it rendered in soft blur. Late-morning sunlight falls from image-left, drawing bright highlights along the robot's galvanized steel edges and casting its long shadow toward image-right across the damp sand. The palette is built from pale tan sand, the muted gray-green blur of sea and foam, the silver-gray of brushed and riveted metal panels, and the matte black of heavy rubber, punctuated by the red, blue and white of scattered litter. The background reads only as broad soft bands of pale surf and hazy light, while the foreground carries crisp detail: rippled wet sand, a ragged line of seaweed, shells and debris marking the tideline, and two dark tire tracks trailing behind the machine. The robot travels toward image-left, its boxy chassis carried on four wide rubber tires whose sidewalls bulge gently under the load and whose treaded contact patches flatten visibly against the sand, grains clinging in the grooves as the wheels press shallow ruts into the surface. At the front of the machine a steel rake with curved tines is engaged with the debris line, lifting a crushed plastic bottle and a tangle of seaweed partway off the beach and onto the lower lip of an inclined mesh conveyor. The conveyor rises diagonally toward image-right between triangular side plates bolted to the chassis with visible hex fasteners, its open-weave belt carried on cross-rollers, stiffened by steel angle struts tying the side rails back to the frame, and driven by a guarded chain at the upper shaft, with pieces of litter riding the belt upward while loose sand falls freely through the mesh in a thin, even shower back onto the beach. At the top of the incline the conveyor discharges its load over the open mouth of a hopper with riveted seams and slightly dented walls mounted between the rear wheels, a dented drink cup caught mid-tumble above the hopper's rim where earlier debris has already gathered in a small mound. The machine sits level and grounded in the frame, the rake leading at image-left, the hopper centered over the axles, an amber beacon glowing on a short mast above the cab housing, and the whole scene reads as documentary industrial realism with crisp mechanical surfaces and a calm, functional working mood.

cosmos500_0022.caption: A square color photograph shows a three-tier serving robot braking mid-aisle in a casual restaurant, captured in a medium eye-level shot with the machine centered and fully in frame, crisp focus across the robot and its cargo, and a deep depth of field that keeps the surrounding dining room legible. Warm ambient light from a row of ceiling-mounted pendant lamps falls from above and slightly in front of the robot, laying soft highlights along the curved edges of its trays and the rim of the juice glass, while a compact shadow pools beneath its base and stretches toward image-right across the floor. The palette pairs the robot's matte white and charcoal-gray shell with the bright orange of the juice, the golden amber of the noodle broth, the pale cream of the stacked plates, and the honey-brown wood-look tile of the aisle. The setting is a straight service aisle running between rows of square dining tables, with light-oak tabletops, black metal chair legs, folded paper menus and small condiment caddies visible on image-left and image-right, and a pale green feature wall with framed prints closing the far end of the room. The robot stands about waist-high on a rounded rectangular base with a slim column rising to a narrow dark display panel at the top, and its chassis is tilting forward in mid-brake, the front edge dipped a few degrees below the rear while both wheels stay grounded, rubber treads pressed flat against the tile in full contact. The top tray holds a full glass of orange juice filled to a finger's width below the rim, the liquid surface staying perfectly level against the tilt of the machine with nothing spilling; the middle tray carries a deep bowl of noodle soup, noodles and broth settled flat inside with a faint wisp of steam rising; the bottom tray supports a neat stack of four white plates. Every item rests squarely on its tray with visible contact between glass, bowl, plates and tray surfaces, and nothing floats or hangs in the air. The robot's forward-leaning posture reads as active deceleration frozen in progress, the column pitched toward the camera while the cargo rides steady above the braking base. The style is clean commercial product photography with realistic materials and true-to-life reflections, and the mood is calm and controlled, the orderly unspilled cargo contrasting with the machine's sudden stop.

cosmos500_0023.caption: A square color photograph captures a six-wheeled sidewalk delivery robot descending a concrete curb ramp in thin winter snow, shot from a low three-quarter side angle at near wheel height with the machine centered and tack-sharp against a softly blurred residential street background. Diffuse midday light from an overcast sky falls evenly from above, casting only faint soft shadows beneath the chassis and picking out bright highlights along the robot's white-and-graphite plastic body panels and the thin white snow covering every flat surface. The palette is dominated by the cool whites and pale grays of snow and concrete, the dark charcoal of the six rubber tires, and one saturated note of fluorescent orange from the triangular safety flag mounted on the whip antenna rising from the robot's rear corner, its fabric fluttering slightly outward as the machine moves. The background dissolves into soft shapes of muted brick facades, a parked silver sedan, and the gray band of the asphalt street, while the foreground shows the ramp's brushed concrete texture, its painted yellow tactile warning strip near the curb edge, and scattered slush collecting along the gutter below. The robot itself is a compact knee-high rectangular chassis with rounded corners, a closed lid, a small dark sensor pod on its front face, and three wheels per side, each a chunky treaded tire on a light gray hub, and all six wheels sit in natural, undistorted contact with the sloped ramp surface, the suspension arms visibly compressed in realistic proportion so the body tilts forward down the incline while the geometry stays coherent and mechanically sound. The front pair of wheels has just rolled past the ramp's lower edge toward the gutter, the middle pair straddles the slope, and the rear pair remains higher on the sidewalk, freezing the descent mid-motion. Behind the robot, six parallel ruts press through the thin snow up the ramp and across the sidewalk, three faintly staggered dark lines per side where the treads have exposed wet gray pavement, trailing the machine in a clean unbroken track that curves gently back toward the top edge of the frame. Small clumps of displaced snow cling to the tire treads and the lower chassis edges, evidence of the wheels actively churning through the dusting rather than resting posed upon it. The style is crisp documentary realism with fine texture in the snow granules, concrete pores and tire rubber, and the mood is quiet and matter-of-fact, a small autonomous machine steadily at work on an ordinary cold morning.

cosmos500_0024.caption: A square color photograph of a wheeled ultraviolet disinfection robot standing beside an empty hospital bed in a clinical ward room, captured in a medium full shot at standing eye level with sharp focus across both machines and a moderately deep depth of field that keeps the nearby wall legible. Cool white light from a grid of recessed ceiling panels falls from above, catching in short bright highlights along the metal guard rods, the curved chrome bed frame and the wheel hubs, while soft grey shadows pool directly beneath the robot's base and the bed's legs on the floor. The palette is dominated by clinical whites and pale greys, with the robot's housing in matte white enamel, its ultraviolet tubes glowing a faint violet-blue at their centers, the bedding a flat hospital white, and the floor a seamless pale grey vinyl with a faint satin sheen that mirrors the ceiling lights in long soft streaks. The background shows a pale blue-grey wall with a horizontal white handrail strip, a medical gas outlet panel with color-coded sockets in green, yellow and blue, a folded privacy curtain on a ceiling track at the far image-left edge, and the edge of a closed white door. The robot occupies image-right of center: a squat rectangular base in white powder-coated steel, barely knee-high, carries four black rubber caster wheels, each one pressed flat at its contact patch against the vinyl with a thin crescent of shadow tucked under the tread, every wheel firmly grounded with none hovering above the floor plane. Rising from the base, four vertical ultraviolet tubes stand in parallel, each seated in a visible white ceramic socket bolted to the top plate of the housing and clamped by a brushed metal retaining collar at its upper end, the whole array enclosed by a welded guard of vertical steel rods spaced evenly around the tubes like a cage. Power cables in black rubber sheathing emerge from a sealed gland fitting on the back of the housing, loop neatly along a clipped channel on the base, and feed into a flush-mounted connection panel beside a small dark touchscreen and a green status indicator, every connector seated with no wire dangling unsupported. To image-left, the empty hospital bed carries a stripped white mattress on a perforated steel platform with its side rails lowered, its four casters also grounded on the vinyl, the bed standing close beside the robot so its frame partially overlaps the guard rods in depth order. The mood is sterile and quietly functional, rendered as a documentary product photograph with precise mechanical realism.

cosmos500_0025.caption: A square color photograph shows a panel-cleaning robot advancing along a tilted photovoltaic panel in a desert solar farm, framed in a medium shot from a low three-quarter angle near the panel's downhill edge, with sharp focus on the robot and glass and a deep depth of field that keeps the rows of panels behind it legible. Harsh midday sunlight pours down from high image-left, glaring in a bright specular streak across the panel glass, flashing along the robot's metal rails, and casting a hard-edged shadow of the machine onto the dusty glass below it and the gravel beneath. The palette is dominated by the deep cobalt blue of the photovoltaic cells, the pale tan and ochre of accumulated dust, the silver of anodized aluminum frames, the sun-bleached grey-brown of the gravel, and a clear cyan desert sky. Behind the main panel, rank after rank of identical tilted panels recede toward a flat horizon, their blue-black faces alternating with pale frames, mounted on grey steel posts driven into gravel ground scattered with small stones and dry tufts of grass beneath a cloudless sky. The robot's wheeled chassis spans the full width of the panel, a low horizontal housing of powder-coated white and safety-orange metal carrying a compact motor enclosure, a recessed sensor strip and stubby axles that end in dark rubber rollers clamped over the silver aluminum frame edges on both sides, the rollers visibly gripping the rails and caught mid-roll. Beneath the chassis, a long brush stretches edge to edge, its dense grey-blue bristles rotating against the glass in firm contact, kicking up a curling sheet of tan dust that the machine is pushing downward off the panel's lower lip, where it falls in mid-air streams onto the gravel. Behind the robot, the clean stripe it is leaving runs the length of its traveled path, the glass there dark, glossy and mirror-sharp, reflecting a band of sky in stark contrast to the matte, dust-filmed blue of the uncleaned section ahead of the brush. The panel tilts at roughly thirty degrees, its lower edge close to the gravel and its upper edge rising toward image-right, with the robot sitting a third of the way up the slope, its chassis parallel to the frame edges and the falling dust partly sliding past the panel lip as it reaches the stones. The image carries the sharp documentary clarity of industrial photography, with fine texture in the gravel, crisp bristle definition on the rotating brush and suspended dust grains in the air, conveying a mood of dry heat, bright exposure and quiet automated labor in an empty landscape.

cosmos500_0026.caption: A square color photograph captures an automated container terminal at dusk, framed in a wide shot from a low three-quarter angle just above the asphalt, with deep depth of field keeping the nearest flat-deck AGV, the towering quay crane and the distant stacks all in sharp focus. The light comes from a fading steel-blue twilight sky banded with a last strip of burnt orange at the horizon and from high sodium floodlights on the crane legs, whose warm amber glow catches wet surfaces and metal edges while soft blue shadows stretch away from each machine, setting a palette of cool slate and indigo against the vivid cobalt blue of the container, the safety yellow of the crane and beacons, and the white and yellow of the painted lane markings. In the background the massive grey steel frame of the quay crane spans the upper half of the image, its horizontal boom reaching over the lane, while rows of stacked containers in rust red, green and grey line the quay edge along image-right, fading into the dimming light. In the foreground, dark wet asphalt fills the lower edge of the frame, its fine aggregate glistening under the floodlights, with shallow puddles pooling along the lane and mirroring the sky. In the midground, beneath the quay crane, the long, low flat-deck AGV carries one blue forty-foot shipping container along the painted lane markings toward image-right, the box's vertically corrugated steel walls and dark cast corner fittings resting on four raised locating cones at the deck corners, with a narrow gap of grey light visible beneath it. The dark grey chassis rides on eight wide rubber tires, four per side, each slightly flattened where it meets the wet asphalt and each caught in mid-roll, with small sensor pods and lit amber beacon lights at the chassis ends. Directly above the moving AGV, the crane's spreader hangs empty, its rectangular steel frame held level, its twistlocks open and its four wire cables drawn taut up into the trolley on the boom. Behind the lead vehicle at image-left, a second identical AGV waits at a painted white stop line with its deck bare and its beacon flashing, while reflections of the yellow beacon lights stretch in long trembling streaks across the puddles between the two machines, reaching toward the stacked containers along the quay edge. The photograph has the crisp, functional clarity of industrial documentary work, with deep dusk saturation and a quiet, automated stillness broken only by the motion of the laden carrier rolling beneath the waiting crane.

cosmos500_0027.caption: A square color photograph of a tracked firefighting robot actively spraying a water jet toward a scorched steel target in a concrete training yard during a firefighting drill, captured in a three-quarter side view from a slightly low camera height near the ground. The focus is sharp across the entire scene with deep depth of field, keeping the robot, the hose, the water arc, and the target all crisply resolved. Late-morning sunlight falls from image-left at a high angle, casting hard-edged shadows of the robot's tracks and chassis onto the concrete toward image-right, while bright highlights glint along the water stream and on the wet metal surfaces. The palette is dominated by the cool gray of the concrete yard, the dark charcoal of the rubber tracks, the safety red of the robot's metal chassis, the black of the thick supply hose, and the white-silver of the sunlit water jet against the brown-black scorched steel of the target. The background shows the far end of the training yard: a weathered concrete perimeter wall, an open metal yard gate at image-right with gray tarmac beyond it, and a pale blue sky above, while the foreground is the stained, water-slicked concrete pad marked with faded yellow training lines. The robot sits slightly image-left of center: a low metal chassis in matte red with riveted panel seams and a small sensor mast, carried between two rubber tracks whose treads press flat and weighted against the concrete with realistic track contact, small puddles compressed beneath the tread edges. Mounted above the body, a swivel water cannon in brushed steel angles upward and toward image-right, its nozzle flaring as a coherent water jet leaves the barrel in a continuous arc, droplets feathering at the stream's edges before the jet strikes the upright scorched steel target near image-right, a rectangular plate blackened and rust-streaked from repeated burns. At the impact point the spray bursts into a fine mist and runs down the plate, collecting in reflective puddles on the concrete beneath it. From the robot's rear coupling, a thick supply hose connects with a visible metal fitting and trails in a smooth curve across the wet concrete toward the yard gate, its ribbed surface glistening. The mood is industrious and controlled, a realistic documentary rendering of training equipment at work with coherent water trajectory and every mechanical part firmly grounded and connected.

cosmos500_0028.caption: A square color photograph shows a quadruped robot climbing a steel staircase inside a logistics warehouse, framed in a medium-wide full-body shot from a three-quarter side angle at the height of the stair flight, with the machine and the treads in sharp focus and the warehouse interior behind them slightly softened. Cool daylight from a row of clerestory windows on image-left mixes with the neutral white of LED high-bay fixtures overhead, catching bright highlights along the robot's top rails, the handrail tubes, and the toolbox lid while soft shadows drop beneath each tread toward image-right. The palette pairs safety yellow and galvanized silver on robot and staircase with the deep gray of the polished concrete floor, the orange uprights of loaded pallet racking, the dull browns of stacked cardboard boxes, and the pale blue-gray of a distant dock door. In the background, steel racking bays rise two stories high, their shelves packed with shrink-wrapped pallets, labeled cartons, and a single blue plastic drum, while a striped yellow-and-black safety column and the loading dock door sit farther back, all muted into softness by the depth of field. The staircase runs diagonally from lower image-left to upper image-right, built from open risers, galvanized diamond-plate treads with yellow nosing strips, tubular steel handrails, and visible bolt heads along the stringers. The robot is a dog-sized machine with a matte safety-yellow central chassis, black anodized leg segments, exposed cabling clipped along each limb, and a compact sensor head of dark glass lenses, and it faces image-right as it actively climbs, its leading front leg raised and bent at the shoulder and knee with its rubber-padded foot hovering a hand's width above the next diamond-plate tread while its other three feet press firmly into the steps below. Its torso is held level against the incline, parallel to the warehouse floor rather than to the stair angle, and strapped flat across its back with two black webbing belts sits a silver aluminum toolbox with riveted seams, rounded corner guards, a hinged top handle, and a pair of polished steel latches facing the camera. The raised leg's knee joint is turned partway through its swing, its foot casts a small crisp shadow on the tread it is reaching toward, and a faint compression shows in the rubber pads of the planted feet, marking the climb as motion in progress rather than a pose. The rendering has the clean, evenly lit realism of industrial editorial photography, and the mood is one of quiet, methodical capability.

cosmos500_0029.caption: A square color photograph of a bipedal humanoid robot walking a muddy ridge at the edge of a rice paddy after rain, captured in a full-body medium shot from a slightly low three-quarter front angle at the robot's chest height, the robot in crisp focus while the flooded fields behind dissolve into a soft blur of colour and light. Diffused daylight filters through the thin overcast sky left behind by the rain, casting cool, even illumination with no hard shadows; bright highlights glide along the robot's wet shoulder shells and the waterlogged path, while a faint soft shadow pools beneath its planted foot. The palette is dominated by jade green rice shoots, silvery gray standing water reflecting the pale sky, and deep chocolate-brown mud, with the robot's matte off-white body and the red lettering on its chest cutting a clean accent through the scene. In the blurred background, terraced paddies step away in soft bands of green and mirror-gray traced by low earthen ridges, a few dark shapes of distant trees hovering under a bright hazy sky, all rendered as gentle washes of colour without fine detail; in the foreground, the ridge path is churned wet mud marked with fresh oval footprints and small puddles holding sky reflections between clumps of flattened grass. The robot stands about the height of an adult person, built from smooth matte off-white panels over charcoal-gray mechanical joints, a rounded head with a single dark horizontal visor band tilted slightly forward, water droplets beading on its glossy shoulder caps. It is mid-stride: the foot nearer image-right presses into the mud, sinking slightly with a wet ridge of earth pushed up around the sole, while the leg nearer image-left swings forward with its knee bent, mud caked around the lifted foot and a small clod dropping away. Both arms are held out level at shoulder height in a straight horizontal line, elbows unlocked and articulated fingers spread for balance, the torso leaning subtly toward the planted side. Across the smooth chest panel, the red Chinese characters "农田助手" are printed in a clean sans-serif typeface, sharply legible against the pale shell, while thin streaks of mud spatter the shin guards and the lower edges of the hip plates as evidence of the walk in progress. The shallow depth of field keeps every mechanical detail crisp against the soft wet landscape, the visual style clean documentary realism carrying a quiet overcast mood of patient, methodical work in a rain-fresh field.

cosmos500_0030.caption: A square documentary color photograph shows a palm-sized hexapod robot moving along a narrow horizontal steel pipe in a research laboratory, framed in a tight side view from a camera set slightly above pipe height so the full body and all six legs sit uncropped inside the frame. Focus is tack-sharp on the robot and the section of pipe it grips, while the background falls into a shallow blur of cool blue-gray and soft white shapes suggesting benches, shelving and equipment with no readable detail. Bright overhead LED panels wash the scene in neutral cool-white light, catching thin specular highlights along each brushed-aluminum leg segment and the pipe's machined surface, with soft shadows pooling directly beneath the body and under the pipe's lower curve. The robot's chassis is a matte charcoal-gray rounded shell the size of an open palm, fastened with small silver screws at its corners, carrying a cluster of dark camera lenses at its front end and a single lit green status LED glowing on its top plate. Six jointed metal legs, three on the near side and three on the far side, grip opposite sides of the pipe: each leg is built from two slim brushed-silver segments hinged at black anodized knee and ankle joints, ending in a ribbed rubber-padded foot that presses visibly against the pipe's curved flanks, the contact points of all six feet clearly readable as small dark pads flattened against the metal. The robot is caught mid-stride in a tripod gait, the front and rear near-side legs planted while the middle near-side leg lifts and reaches forward along the pipe, so the body stays level and balanced with every limb evenly spaced and no legs crossing, overlapping or intersecting. A thin black braided cable plugs into a port on the robot's belly and dangles beneath its body, hanging in a loose U-shaped curve below the pipe and swaying slightly outward, its free end dropping toward the bottom edge of the frame.
